rationale: Paracetamol can potentiate the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin at regular doses; monitor INR closely.
Concurrent heavy alcohol use increases the risk of hepatotoxicity with Paracetamol.
Aspirin enhances anticoagulant effect and can cause GI bleeding; combination requires close medical supervision.
NSAIDs can reduce the cardioprotective effect of low-dose aspirin; stagger dosing or avoid combination.
Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis when taken with Metformin; avoid concurrent use.
Combining two fluoroquinolones increases risk of QT interval prolongation and serious cardiac arrhythmias.
Bacteriostatic-bactericidal antagonism possible; clinical significance is debated but typically avoided in serious infections.
Concurrent use of two QT-prolonging antibiotics greatly increases risk of Torsades de Pointes.
Combined CNS depression; drowsiness, impaired coordination and respiratory depression risk are increased.
Two benzodiazepines together markedly increase CNS depression, respiratory depression, and overdose risk.
Opioid-benzodiazepine combination substantially increases risk of respiratory depression and death.
Tramadol combined with antihistamines can cause excessive sedation and lower the seizure threshold.
Combined use increases CNS and respiratory depression; lowest effective doses should be used if combination is required.
Metformin may reduce absorption of Levothyroxine; separate doses by at least 4 hours.
Fluoroquinolones can cause severe hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia in patients taking sulfonylureas; monitor blood glucose.
PPIs may modestly reduce Metformin absorption; dose separation or monitoring may be warranted in sensitive patients.
Additive sedation; patients should be warned against driving or operating machinery.
Azithromycin may increase Fexofenadine plasma levels via P-gp inhibition; monitor for prolonged sedation.
Cephalosporins may potentiate the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin; INR monitoring is recommended.
Generally considered safe; however combining analgesics increases risk of GI side effects and should be time-limited.
